To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

neurons in rat somatosensation cortex (S1) respond to wavefronts of moving whisker deflection by showing suppression of responses to the whisker that is first deflected in the wavefront, and that this suppression is independent of wavefront velocity.
the responses of neurons in S1 of rats to wavefronts of moving whisker deflection depend strongly on the position at which the wavefronts initiate and the direction they move.

the neural response to the principal whisker (the whisker that evokes the strongest response) is suppressed by the responses to other whiskers when they are deflected in rapid sequence, but not when the principal whisker is deflected alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the representation of naturalistic sensory inputs in the brain.
the representation of natural somatosensation in the primary somatosensory (SI) cortex.
understanding how natural sensory stimuli are represented in the brain and, in particular, how the somatosensory system processes information about object texture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
moving wavefronts generate a complex pattern of neural responses in SI that reflect the specific sequence of whisker deflections that comprise a wavefront.
the somatosensory system has evolved to process the natural whisker motion of rats.

moving wavefronts, consisting of sequences of deflections of multiple whisker arcs, are represented as a series of temporally overlapping and spatially overlapping events, which are processed in a manner that is consistent with the known functional architecture of the barrel column.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the representation of moving whisker wavefronts in rat S1 is dominated by the starting arc and is largely independent of the direction of the wavefront.
the neural response to a single whisker deflection is modulated by the deflection history of the other whiskers.
wavefronts of sequential deflections are represented by a sequence of SW and subsequent PW deflections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
wavefront direction selectivity reflects differential responses to specific whisker deflections, which may be useful for identifying the location and direction of object features.
wavefronts of natural whisker deflection generate highly selective and robust responses in rat somatosensation.
the brain represents whisker deflections in the form of a sequence of whisker deflections, rather than a single deflection.
